answer: In an agent economy, each new identity must first mint a ferrous stake bond locked for several epochs before it can vote or claim rewards. Bonds are tied to a public work cipher derived from recent challenges, so cloned bots cannot reuse one proof across many labels. Peers also demand a short sonnet-length rationale that cites unique on-ledger receipts; farms paying per head then face rising capital and uniqueness costs that blunt sybil waves.
